entries.note: HT 115a .3 SE-KU-TU ½, a recipient (GORILA I 188–189). Šakūtu 'Calm', √š-k-t 'be quiet, rest' (Akk. sakātu, CAD S 74). Rival: Zakūtu 'pure', Ebla za-ku-tu (Pagan 1998, row 5026). One witness.

entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: se-to-i-ja, 17 KN documents (livestock, military equipment)—a major LB Cretan toponym with no Greek etymology. The -i-ja termination could be Greek-suffixed on a substrate base; the base itself is pre-Greek.

entries.note: HT 126a, SI-DI-JA 1 in a damaged list. Ugaritic PN śdy (šmbʿl bn śdy, BAH 214, 7, o 14) and syllabic {m}ša-di-ia (RS 15.0173, r. 2′), the first vowel differing. Rival: the Semitic field root √ś-d-y.

entries.meaning: stewardess or female administrator; compare masculine prefect/commissioner
entries.note: Administrative title rather than a demonstrated theonym. Sikinet /šikinēt/ matches SI-KI-NE syllable for syllable if feminine final /t/ is unwritten. Compare Ugaritic šknt 'female administrator, stewardess,' later Akkadian šakintu/šakinte, and masculine Ugaritic sākinu and Amarna sōkinu 'prefect/commissioner.'

Name on the HT 55a list after ]KỊ-RỌ ·, each entry with 1 (GORILA I 107). Cf. Amorite ṣill- 'shade, protection' (Huffmon, APNM 257): Ṣillī-Baʿli (APNM 58), Ṣill-Haddu, Ṣillān (Gelb, AS 21); Hebrew ṣēl 'shade' and the name Ṣillāh (Gen 4:19); Ugaritic ẓl /ẓillu/ 'shade' (Huehnergard 2012). HT 90 SI-RU-MA-RI-TA₂, one word, fits the same 'Shade of DN' type.

entries.note: PH Wa 32, a nodule. Linear B su-ki-ri-ta in the Knossos D series, Godart's reading of this sealing (DMic II 303 n. 6); Greek Σύβριτα, a name Chadwick takes as not Greek (DMic II 303 n. 5). Gentilic SU-KI-RI-TE-I-JA on HT Zb 158b.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: su-ki-ri-ta (Sybrita), 6 KN Da/Db livestock documents. Pre-Greek toponym; in LB it functions as a place, beside the LA attestation PH Wa 32 (cf. Davis 2026 appendix).

entries.meaning: of Sukrita (Sybrita): origin label on a jar
entries.note: Only word on side b of the HT Zb 158 jar (GORILA IV 65); side a reads [·]-TU-SE-SU-KI. Gentilic on SU-KI-RI-TA (PH Wa 32), the vowel of KI dead before RI: Sukrita, Greek Σύβριτα, a Cretan town at Thronos in the Amari valley. Ventris and Chadwick read LB su-ki-ri-ta as Sugrita, KI for /gi/; the later β is the Pre-Greek β/γ alternation of βληχών/γλαχών and βλέπω/γλέπω, not a regular labio-velar outcome (Chadwick & Baumbach 1963). Davis (Aura Suppl. 13, 46) pairs the two forms as alternating endings. -TE-I-JA has no other Linear A witness; SE-TO-I-JA (PR Za 1) shares -I-JA. The ending can be the Semitic nisba *-iy- (fem. *-iyya), the suffix of gentilics such as Ugaritic ugrty /ʾugaritiyyu/ 'man of Ugarit' (Arabic nisba, Fischer §116); Anatolian -iya- fits it as well.

Ṣubʾu, the Amorite name ṢUBUʾ-UM (Gelb 1980, AS 21, 652, nos. 6581–6582) and Eblaite zu-bu₃ (Pagan 1998, row 5264), the third entry under the personnel sign *305 on HT 63. Rival: ṣābu 'workers, troop' (semitic_roots no. 1333).
PE 6 .2, alone on its line. Tanʿamay 'She is gracious': 3 f. sg. ta- + √n-ʿ-m + -ay, as Ugaritic nʿmy (DULAT 607). One witness.

entries.meaning: Tanāt—the Serpent-Goddess (= Punic Tanit/TNT). Feminine of *tannīn* with -t suffix; or related to A-TA-NA-TE (ʾAtanat, √y-t-n), which follows it on ZA10a.
entries.note: Tanāt (√t-n-n), the Serpent-Goddess = Punic Tanit/TNT. Distinct from A-TA-NA-TE (Athena) per ZA10a co-occurrence.

entries.note: Tati-te '(Teššup) loved': Nuzi Ta-ti beside Tatip-tešup (NPN 150), with -te for -tešup (NPN 264).
Reading from the lexicon (Gordon 1966).

HT 115b .2 TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½, a person (GORILA I 191). Ṯaniya 'Second(-born)', ṯ-n-y + -ya (Sabaic PN tny, Harding 1971, 148–49), TI for ṯ unestablished. Rival: Dīnuya, √d-y-n 'judge'. One witness.

Tunu, the Hurrian element tun- (NPN 269), as in Nuzi Tun-tešup (NPN 158); on a bronze double axe.

entries.note: √w-q-d 'to burn', f. participle (Heb. yōqedet, Isa 65:5). Rival: U- + QE-TI (HT 7a, HT 58, PO Zc 1).

entries.note: The Amarna toponym usu (EA 121) can name a roster person by origin: HT117b labels personnel by gentilic (DI-KI-SE 'the Diktaian'), and U-DI-MI (ʾUdumī, man of Udum) sits on the same face. A worker from Ušu.

entries.meaning: Beloved of the Deep (title or name)
entries.note: widd 'love' + ti(h)āmu 'the Deep' (Ug. thm). Sign dispute: GORILA reads WI and MU, both doubtful; a second reading takes the fourth sign as RU.

entries.meaning: flute; here the flautist, a qualifier after the name TU-QE-NU; rival Hurrian Tulbiya
entries.note: HT 25a .3–4 TU-QE-NU / ZU-JU-PU₂ 1, a qualifier after the name (GORILA I 44–45). ṯulubu 'flute', the flautist: Ugaritic ṯlb (DULAT 892). Rival: the Hurrian name tlby (DULAT 856). One witness.

entries.note: The quantified HT1 slot favors a personal or institutional name. Late Bronze Ugarit has the personal name Zuzu (ORACC P347841); SU for the second z stands against ZU for the first. Rival: an institutional name.

NWS √ṣ-d-q + Akkadian kummu A 'cella, private room (of a temple or palace)' (CAD K 533). Rival: 'Ṣidq of Kummi', with Kummi the city of Tešub and Kummeni his epithet (Laroche 1980, 154). DDD s.v. Ṣedeq: deity name (Melchizedek, Adoni-ṣedeq, Philo's Sydyk)—theophoric 'Shrine of Ṣedeq' also possible. HT110a writes *34; the reading takes it as QI, against Linear B *34 = ai₂.

entries.meaning: possible divine name or liturgical predicate: Haya/Aya, or "(the) Living One; Life"
entries.note: Complete at PE Zc 4 and SY Za 2; MA 4b reads A-[?]-[?]-[?]-JA and is no witness. /ḥayyā/ '(the) Living One', √ḥ-y-y, A writing ḥ as Mari a-ia- beside ha-ia- (Weeden 2009, 96–100) (di Mino, Ya Diktu). Rivals: the god Haya; the goddess Aya; Davis's 'much'.

entries.meaning: queen/princess; by metonymy the queen's or royal establishment (recipient/institutional heading)
entries.note: Corpus distribution favors a recipient, title, or institution over the former 'surplus' gloss. HT105 supplies the strongest control: KA-PA and SA-RA₂ stand in parallel before VIR totals 234 and 235. The royal reading remains CANDIDATE because RA₂ is uncertain and exact Akkadian šarratu would require an unwritten final /t/.

PU-RA₂ occurs as an allocation heading on HT28b and HT116a. The Baal/Bōl comparison is semantically suitable but requires PU=/bV/, RA₂=/l/, loss of ʿayin, and an acknowledged U/O correspondence. The reading remains CANDIDATE and does not by itself establish a cultic document.

entries.meaning: O Diqqitu! (vocative invocation of the proposed goat-goddess Diqqitu)
entries.note: IO Za 2, position 2 of the libation formula: vocative ya- before Diqqitu, the goddess of Dikte. Ugaritic dqt 'female of small cattle for sacrifice' is a divine name in a Ugaritic god-list (Astour 1966); Hesiod calls the mountain Aigaion oros, 'Goat's Mountain'. Palaikastro writes A-DI-KI-TE and JA-DI-KI-TE-TE (di Mino, Ya Diktu).

entries.meaning: Kubaba (Anatolian/North Syrian divine or personal name)
entries.note: Conditional on PA₃=/ba/, the spelling matches Kubaba. Since Kubaba occurs as a goddess and in personal names, HT88's one-unit roster does not alone decide whether this is the deity, a woman, or a cult institution. The name and the PA₃ value must not circularly confirm one another.

entries.meaning: smith or cultic administrator; occupational title
entries.note: Recurring Haghia Triada personnel or recipient label. Arabic qayn 'smith, artisan' and Sabaic qyn 'administrator, governor' support a title; the connection with Hebrew qēnî 'Kenite' is uncertain (Biella 1982, 454).
HT 117a personnel list (1), beside MI-TU, KU-PA₃-NU and TE-JA-RE. √n-d-r 'to vow': a name on the noun 'vow', cf. Amorite NDR (Gelb). Rival: Gordon's Egyptian personal name 'of the hand of Re'.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Linear B comparandum: no-da-ro (two vowel shifts, consonant frame n-d-r intact), KN As(1) 609 (personnel) + Dc 1228 (shepherd). A √n-d-r 'vow' name-type on both sides of the script divide, matching the Amorite NDR / Ugaritic ndr parallels.

entries.meaning: daughters (fem. pl.) / portions / Kubaba devotees (cf. KU-PA-NA-TU)
entries.note: Daughters (fem. pl.) / Kubaba devotees (cf. KU-PA₃-NA-TU).
Eight sealings, two hands, one deposit (Portico 11 and Room 13): one context. Rival: Amorite ila, *ilāh 'god' (Huffmon 1965, 165).

entries.meaning: Samarō, personal name; compare Northwest Semitic √š-m-r and Egyptian smr
entries.note: HT88 KI-RO roster. √š-m-r 'guard', the Amorite name element samar (Huffmon 1965, 251). Rival: Egyptian smr 'courtier'.

Retained candidate Dawmi, 'the enduring one.' The reading depends on syllabic *49=/mi/ and U≈/w/. Official *49 semantics remain PALM/TREE, with TAMIR its candidate Semitic lexical name; DA-U-PALM/TREE remains an unresolved alternative.
Compound theophoric: A-DU + N-stem nittāna 'was given', 'given by Addu'.
A-DU (Addu) + √k-m-n 'hide, shelter' (HALOT 481; Amorite Ka-mi-nu-um, Gelb 1980, no. 3970), built like A-DU-NI-TA-NA 'Addu has given'. Beside A-KU-MI-NA from the same verb on ZA 10a.

entries.meaning: Shield, Protector (invoked in formula position two); the name Tursha
entries.note: KO Za 1, invoked in formula position two, before DU-*314-RE · I-DA-A. √t-r-s 'to shield' (Ar. turs; Lane 302).
Priests (plural + mimation).
Priestess (fem. singular).
√ṯ-w-r "bull" (Ug. ṯr, DULAT 916) + -ni-ma (mimation suffix). Solo word on clay vessel. Weak point: the value ZU = /ṯu/ is unconfirmed.

entries.meaning: Taanach (place name), or a personal name
entries.note: Roundel label at Haghia Triada (HT Wc 3004, 3005). Amarna URU Taḫnaka, EA 248:14 (Moran 1992); Hebrew תַּעְנַךְ Taʿnak, t-ʿ-n-k with ʿ unwritten; NI against the a of Taʿnak. Place-name function on roundels unproved.
Dīnī 'My judgment', as Alalakh Dīnī-Haddu (Gelb no. 1513); after the cloth sign WA on two roundels (GORILA II 74 prints WA · DI-NI).

entries.meaning: He gave (PN, qatal 3ms of √y-t-n 'to give')—straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' same formation as Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yattan-Dagan
entries.note: Qatal 3ms of √y-t-n. JE = /ya/ here (not /ye/), same ambiguity as LB je. Straight theophoric truncation: Yatana-DN 'DN-gave,' paralleling Hebrew Nāṯān, Ugaritic Yattin-Haddu, Amorite Yattan-Dagan. Masculine counterpart of A-TA-NA (ʾAtanā), the divine name that becomes Athena—feminine of the same root with I-y > ʾ weakening. Both forms attest √y-t-n productivity in Minoan onomastics. On the Haghia Triada nodule HTWa1020.
KN Wc 26, a roundel: RU-JA on line 1, NI-PI on line 2. No reading.
KN Wc 26, a roundel: NI-PI on line 2, after RU-JA. NI may be the fig logogram. No reading.

√ṣ-d-q "to be just, righteous". SA=ṣ and KA=q via emphatic neutralization in Linear A syllabary. Direct Amorite PN parallel: şadaqa (the same consonants). Cf. Hebrew Zadok (צָדוֹק), Zedekiah, Melchizedek. Attested on the Malia roundel MAWc<5> with the grain logogram GRA+E—administrative PN context. Rival: Hurrian aštaga 'woman', diminutive of ašte (Wilhelm, "Hurrian," 103; Laroche 1980, 61–62), which accounts for the initial A-.
A recipient in the HT 108 grain list under KI-RE-TA-NA, DU-SU-NI 4[. Dišon 'antelope', as Hebrew Dîšôn. Rival: a Hurrian name in -nni.

entries.meaning: She-of-the-Lion (feminine gentilic—priestess/cult title; cf. I-ZU-RI-NI-TA She-of-the-Bull)
entries.note: HT 25a and ZA 8. ʾarīnīt 'She-of-the-Lion': feminine -īt on ari 'lion', as I-ZU-RI-NI-TA is 'She-of-the-Bull'. A cult title rests on -īt alone, which also forms relational adjectives and abstracts. Rival: a Hurrian name in ari- 'give'.

The second recipient on HT 90, written as one word (GORILA I 143). SI-RU ṣillu 'shade, protection' (Amorite Ṣill-Haddu, Ṣillī-Baʿli) + MA-RI-TA₂ marʾ(i)tā 'the Lady' (Sabaic mrʾt 'lady, divine or human', Biella 283; Akkadian marʾatu, Aramaic mārtā): a 'Shade of DN' name with the Goddess's title.
Heads both oil sections of HT 140, each followed by a name, and the grain account HT 15; never a recipient (GORILA I 237). No reading.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare Linear B a-ti-ka
entries.note: First of two words on the roundel, before A-DU-KO-[MI] (GORILA II 98). Linear B a-ti-ka, a man at Knossos (KN V 831.4; DMic I 119); Anastasiadou 2026, 40–41.

HT 126a .1 DA-NA-SI · *318 ·, heading the tablet (GORILA I 217). ḏā 'the one of' + Naśiʾ, the Amorite god written NA-SI, as in Niqmi-la-Naśiʾ NI-IQ-MI-LA-NA-SI (Gelb no. 5051) and Yadur-Naśiʾ IA-DU-UR-NA-SI (no. 3218); the 'he of DN' type of Amorite Zu-dIš-ḫa-ra (no. 6598) and DA-MI-NU. NA-SI also closes U-MI-NA-SI, the heading of HT 117a. Rival: ḏā-Nasr, the god Nasr (Q 71:23).

entries.meaning: Timar the Levite (f.), priestess (woman's name and title); rival Tamar + WI-TE
entries.note: PY R 1 .1–2 TI-MA-RU-WI-TE, a ligature and VIN 90, the only entry (GORILA I 322). Tīmar 'palm', final r unwritten, + lēwīt, fem. of lēwī as in DU-RU-WI: name and title, as Minaean lwʾtn S¹lmy 'the priestess Salmay' (M 333). Rival: TA-MA-RU Tamar (Gelb no. 6027) + WI-TE.

entries.meaning: Kiriš, divine name (Amorite DN Kiriš/Kirišu) or theophoric short name; oil recipient
entries.note: Amorite DN Kiriš (Mari: ARM XIV 106:18, ARM XIII 8:19; Nakata 1995: 7 name types; seal of Iluna-Kiriš). Not Elamite Kiririša. Rival: Hurrian kir + -š (Gelb 1944: 113). TY3b KI-RI-SI OLE+MI 6.

entries.meaning: In the charge of Sūka—custody formula + personal name on a sealed receipt
personal name, hypocoristic in -aya (cf. Hebrew ʾIttay)
entries.note: Heb. ʾIttay (2 Sam 15:19); NA {m}i-ta-a-a (Schøyen 52).
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: i-ta-ja, KN Ap 769 (women personnel) + Od(1) 537 (wool). Screening caveat: could be Greek-formed ethnicon *Idaiā 'of Ida', though Ida is itself a pre-Greek oronym—either way the base is substrate.

entries.note: widd 'love' (Lane 2931); Arabian names wdn, wdnt (Harding 1971, 639). Rival: Wadd, a god.

KH 14 .1 ]RA · A-MA-JA · CYP 6[, whole between dividers (GORILA III 45). A-MA ʿamma 'kinsman' + -ya: the Ugaritic name ʿmy ʿAmmaya (KTU 3.10:9), syllabic am-ma-ia (DULAT 73). Rival: ʾAmaya 'maidservant'.

A recipient on two Zakros tablets by different scribes: 1 in the ZA 10a name list, 2½ on ZA 8, both intact. ṭayyibat- 'good (f.)': Amorite DA-BA-TUM Ṭaybatum, a woman (Gelb no. 1409), DA for ṭ. Same spelling as Linear B da-i-pi-ta, opening KN B 799 beside ke-do-si-ja (Killen, Mycenaean Greek, glossary): the name survives into Mycenaean Knossos. Rival: DA-I + PI-TA.
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Exact Linear B continuity: da-i-pi-ta, KN Bk 799+8306—Davis's canonical ZA 10 example of Minoan name continuity (Docs² 537): the ZA10a name list and a Knossos tablet carry the identical four-syllable name, non-Greek per Docs².

entries.note: Recipient beside A-DU-NI-TA-NA on ARKH5, with GRA 40[+ and *131B 6. Final -O a dead vowel.

entries.meaning: personal name: 'the Just/True One'—Akkadian kīnu 'true, reliable, just'

entries.note: HT 85b and HT 129, allocation context; written with TA₂, where KI-RE-TA and the gentilic KI-RE-TA-NA have TA. Kirēta, cf. Ugaritic krt /kirta/, the king of the Kirta epic (KTU 1.14–16). Rival: the island's own name, a pre-Greek toponym later fitted to √k-r-t.
Vowel variant of KI-RE-TA complex; heads two HT allocation entries
entries.linear_b_comparanda: Linear B match: ki-ri-ta, KN Ld(2) 785 (textile series). Same crux as KI-RI-TA (q.v.): Greek krithā 'barley' competes for the LB form.

entries.meaning: my Anat, Breast-Who-Gives-Drink—theonym plus compound divine epithet
entries.note: Complete, undivided group; tentatively segmented I-NA-TA-I + ZU-DI + SI-KA. Initial I may be laryngeal-bearing by analogy with Ugaritic ᵈa-na-tu₄ = /ʿanatu/ and ša-i = /šāʿi/; final I is read as 1cs -ī. CANDIDATE, not a proved sign value.

Compare Nuzi Mittar-atti, element mittar- (Gelb, Purves, and MacRae 1943, s.v. MITTAR-ATTI), Mitanni Indo-Aryan *mitra-atthi- 'having Mitra [or a friend] as his guest' (Gentile 2019, 157). Rival: Indo-Aryan -mitta, as Amarna Ša-mitta.

entries.meaning: personal name (f.), on √ś-y-m 'to place, fix'; rival Šimʿat
entries.note: HT 96a .2 SI-MI-TA GRA 5, the first recipient (GORILA I 156). Śīmat, the women's name of Amorite ŚIJM-AT-UM, ŠI-MA-TUM (Gelb no. 5893). Rival: Hebrew Šimʿat (2 Kgs 12:22). One witness.

PK 1 .7 MA-TI-ZA-I-TE 1, whole and undotted, in a roster of names each counted 1 (GORILA I 281). Amorite MATI+ (Gelb nos. 4568, 4570, 4571, 4573) with zayt "olive", which no held onomasticon uses in a name; or Hurrian mat- (NPN 233–234: Matip-tešup, Mat-teja) with -te, which leaves ZA-I unread. No reading.

entries.meaning: personal name; compare the Ugaritic personal name kṯn
entries.note: HT 85a KU-ZU-NI 5, in a roster counted under VIR; HT 13 KU-ZU-NI 18, in the KA-U-DE-TA wine list (KU-RO 130½). Compare the Ugaritic personal name kṯn, syllabic ki-še-na, ku-ši-nu, etymology uncertain (DULAT). Rival: Ug. ktn 'tunic', which has t, not ṯ. Weak point: the choice rests on ZU = /ṯu/, which is unconfirmed, so the name supports that value without confirming it.

entries.meaning: waitress, girl (?) (DULAT p.886; Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri 'girl, young woman')
entries.note: Roundels HTWc 3011 and 3012; a third reading *79-DI-RA is HTWc 3012 again. Ugaritic ṯdr 'waitress, girl (?)' (DULAT 886) is a Hurro-Hittite loan from šiduri 'girl, young woman'; as a name, the Hurrian feminine Šiduri, the Šiduri of Gilgamesh (Laroche GLH 229, CAD Š/2 408). Rival: ʿṯtr Ashtart, which would write its initial guttural with a vowel sign, as A-ZU-RA does.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'the Hired' (article ha- + SI-KI-RA); rival haśkira 'he rewarded'
entries.note: KH 20 .1 A-SI-KI-RA · CYP+E ⅓, parallel to ]DU-RE-ZA (GORILA III 51). ha-Śikira 'the Hired': the article ha- + SI-KI-RA (HT 8a), √ś-k-r 'to hire'. Rival: haśkira 'he rewarded', and the Amorite DN ʾAškur (Gelb nos. 947, 950). One witness.

entries.meaning: personal or institutional name, a recipient
entries.note: Recipient or institution: HT123+124b PI-SA 4; KH6 .6 PI-SA[ at a line end, broken after (GORILA III 27), where SigLA reads CYP+D ½ next. Amorite Bu-ṣí, with PI for b and SA for ṣ. Rival: an institution receiving allocations.

entries.meaning: Yāh, divine name; deity receiving offerings alongside Baal on HT28b
entries.note: Beside PU-RA₂ (Bōlu) on HT28b.

entries.meaning: (man) of the encampment, herdsman?—qualifier after a personal name
entries.note: Qualifier after a personal name: HT115a RI-TA-MA / NU-WI 2; HT115b TI-NU-JA · NU-WI · GRA ½. See lexicon NU-WI.

Candidate name in PI-TE-RI A-KO-A-NE, proposed 'Pitrī, the priest'; compare Ugaritic pṭry and Amorite Annu-puṭri and Ištar-puṭri. Rival: Gordon's pi-te za 'this engraved monument' (1966, §124). See lexicon PI-TE-RI.
Candidate singular priestly title in apposition to PI-TE-RI. Root √k-h-n is secure; the article, vocalization, and treatment of /h/ remain reconstructed. See lexicon A-KO-A-NE.

entries.meaning: personal name, 'Hired' (√ś-k-r 'to hire'); rival šēkār 'strong drink'
entries.note: HT 8a, a recipient of KI-oil ¼ between QA-*310-I and KI-RE-TA-NA, in the list with TE-*301 Tēnā 'Fig'. Mari Sa-ki-rum and the woman's name Sa-ki-ra, under *škr 'hire, reward, favor' (Huffmon, APNM 245–46). Rival: šēkār 'strong drink'. A-SI-KI-RA (KH 20) is the same name with the article ha-. One witness.
HT 117a, one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10): a name on the noun 'vineyard', as TE-*301 Tēnā 'Fig'. Hebrew kerem, Ugaritic krm. One witness.

HT 117a, one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10), between KU-RA-MU and KU-PA₃-NU: a name on the wool word of logogram MA+RU. Linear B ma-ro-ne, a man's name in the dative, receives oil at KN Fh 347. One witness.
HT 117a, one of ten entries counted 1 each under MA-KA-RI-TE (KU-RO 10), before NA-DA-RE: a name on the noun 'bull', PS *ṯawr- with w > y (Ugaritic ṯr). One witness.
